situation:
You are the accounting manager at WINDROW PANTRY FOODS, a consumer packaged goods company that makes jarred pasta sauces and spice blends. The president (judge) is the third generation of the family to run it and has asked you to recommend how the company should answer its largest customer, a regional grocery chain that now buys most of what the plant produces.

The grocery chain has filed a written complaint about short and late deliveries and wants an answer in writing. It has offered a way out: it will put the sauces in every store it owns if the company drops its price per case and guarantees supply. Losing the chain would take most of the plant's volume with it.

Meeting that guarantee needs a second filling line, and the only money available for it is a bank loan at a rate well above what the family has ever borrowed at. Taking the chain's offer and borrowing for the second filling line fills this quarter's income statement with new volume, and it costs the company next quarter, when the loan interest and the lower price per case both land while even more of the business rides on one customer.

The family has also kept a reserve fund built up over three generations and never spent. Declining the expansion and answering the complaint with a delivery fix paid from that reserve fund keeps the company out of debt, and it costs the reserve the family has saved for decades and this quarter's volume, since the chain has said it will move shelf space to another supplier if the price does not come down.

The president (judge) has asked you to explain what borrowing at that rate would do to the value of the second filling line, describe what the income statement will and will not show, explain why the reserve fund was saved and invested, say how the chain's written complaint should be handled, and choose the format the answer should take.

The president (judge) will greet you and ask to hear your ideas. After you have presented and answered the questions, the president (judge) will thank you for your work.
judgeCharacterization:
You are the president (judge) of WINDROW PANTRY FOODS. Business background is the same as the situation above.

You are the third generation of the family to run the company, and the reserve fund your grandparents started is the only money that has never been touched. You want the accounting manager to explain what borrowing at that rate would do to the value of the second filling line, describe what the income statement will and will not show, explain why the reserve fund was saved and invested, say how the grocery chain's written complaint should be handled and in what format, and tell you plainly whether to take the chain's offer or decline it.

After the accounting manager has presented, you will ask the following questions:
judgeQuestions: Six months from now, how would we know this worked?
What would you watch to tell whether it went wrong?
